claims.statement: Following the 2026 AI Omnibus, Annex III high-risk AI rules are scheduled for 2 December 2027 and product-embedded high-risk rules for 2 August 2028.
The Commission lists risk management, data quality, logging, documentation, human oversight, robustness, cybersecurity, and accuracy among high-risk obligations.
The Commission states that conformity assessment may require an independent body for some systems and that harmonized AI standards remain under development.

contrary_evidence: The 2026 timeline extension delays compulsory high-risk demand.
Some conformity assessments require authorized independent bodies, so this business may remain a subcontractor or pre-assessment service.

economics.acquisition_route: Counsel and security-assessment referrals, then buyer-mandated vendor assessments
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Illustrative, unvalidated path: 100 clients averaging 60000 PLN annual revenue could create 6m PLN revenue; at 30% operating margin and 75% founder ownership, a profit-based valuation could plausibly exceed 5m PLN around year 5-6
economics.founder_time: 4 hours/day initially, with legal interpretation and domain experts contracted
economics.gross_margin_basis: Target 60-75% after specialist review, compute, quality assurance, insurance, and sales partner fees
economics.payback: Unvalidated: two full assessments plus one monitoring contract could cover initial build cost within 12 months
economics.pricing: Unvalidated: 20000-80000 PLN per assessment plus 5000-15000 PLN per quarter for monitored releases
economics.retention_or_repeat: New models, datasets, and releases trigger retesting; enterprise evidence contracts can renew annually

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Proprietary benchmark cases, failure corpus, accepted report format, and historical evidence across versions
fingerprint.customer: EU AI vendors and deployers in employment, education, finance, and other sensitive workflows
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Partnerships with AI counsel, security assessors, procurement advisors, and selected enterprise buyers
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Independent technical tests, reproducible evidence pack, remediation queue, and release monitoring; not legal certification
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: Provider or deployer pays per assessment and quarterly or release-based monitoring
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A high-impact AI system enters procurement, changes model or data, or approaches a compliance milestone

founder_fit: Directly uses data science, AI, experimentation, and documentation discipline
Service can begin manually before tooling is automated
Enterprise referrals reduce dependence on public-facing content
Capital needs are primarily labor and secure compute
risks: Unauthorized certification language could create regulatory exposure
Standards and implementation dates can change
Large assurance firms can bundle testing with legal and audit services

structure.commercial_archetype: Independent testing lab with recurring version-monitoring contracts
structure.control_point: A buyer-accepted, version-bound test packet embedded in procurement and model-change approval
structure.critical_dependency: Major buyers, insurers, or authorized conformity bodies must accept the test protocol as useful evidence

thesis: Build a technically rigorous pre-conformity evidence service for EU employers and other sensitive-use AI vendors: dataset tests, robustness and bias suites, logging checks, human-oversight exercises, and a version-bound evidence packet that a buyer can require before procurement. It must not claim statutory certification unless separately authorized.
title: Procurement-Grade AI Evidence Lab
uncertainties: Which buyer will make the report a mandatory gate
Whether clients will expose models and sensitive datasets
Whether harmonized standards will commoditize the testing suite
